observation_summary: The CompressorStreamFactory fails to detect deflate streams that contain a zlib header, resulting in a CompressorException when attempting to open such streams.
hypothesis: The detection logic in CompressorStreamFactory is missing a check for the zlib header signature, and the DeflateCompressorInputStream class lacks a static method to identify this signature.
prediction: Adding a 'matches' method to DeflateCompressorInputStream and calling it within the detection logic of CompressorStreamFactory will allow the factory to correctly identify and handle these streams.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the addition of a 'matches' method in DeflateCompressorInputStream and a corresponding call in CompressorStreamFactory, which directly implements the missing detection capability.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic omission where the system lacked the logic to identify a specific file format (deflate with zlib header). This is not a simple guard (Checking) or a wrong value (Assignment), but a missing procedural step in the detection algorithm. It is not a design-level capability (Function/Class/Object) because the infrastructure for handling streams already existed; it just needed the specific detection logic added to the existing method.
evidence_used: CompressorStreamFactory.java diff adding a call to DeflateCompressorInputStream.matches
DeflateCompressorInputStream.java diff adding the static matches method and magic constants
Bug report description stating the factory doesn't handle deflate streams with a zlib header

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is a local procedural addition to existing classes rather than a design-level change or the addition of a new major capability.
While it involves a check, the primary issue is the absence of the detection algorithm itself, not just a missing guard on existing data.
